journal:
I don't think anybody knew who he actually was, and im sure he was glad of it. I remember him telling me later on in the night that he'd traded shirts with one of the stable lads to "rough" himself up a bit. Of course when a handsome young stanger swaggers in to one of the the city's, less than desirable drinking establishments he tends to stick out, but after losing his first few games of dice they stopped caring where it was from as the wealth started to pass around.

I remember there was a grizzled hermit looking fella who started calling him Rob, and then the name just sorta stuck, I don't remember anybody actually asking his name, he didn't seem to mind. He had such a raucous energy to him by the end of the night, like a thousand responsibilities had been lifted from his shoulders and he was enjoying the first night of his life as a free man.

He'd come and visit a few more times over the years, each time was a night to remember, I remember after the coronation he didn't visit any more, so I suppose that's that, I'm pretty sure somebody; it might even have been him, carved a little crown onto the underside of one of the tables with "Rob" scrawled next to it.
prompt: A handsome young prince disguised in plain clothes plays dice games in the tarvern with the townsfolks, happy and jovial

music.why: A raucous medieval tavern night of dice with a disguised prince, recalled fondly by someone who knows he stopped coming after the coronation, calls for a warm but looking-back feel with folk-village instruments.
